threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You don't flinch at the sound of the train screeching overhead during brunch in Dalston. It's part of the atmosphere, not a nuisance.
Last week I saw a bloke in a onesie, juggling apples, while the bus was stuck at the Brixton roundabout. Only in London, right?

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I spotted a guy walking his pet iguana along Weserstraße, I realized this place thrives on the unexpected.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you find a kebab shop that serves döner with homemade curry sauce. It’s a late-night treasure that locals swear by.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know someone’s a local when they still ride BART despite the delays, but complain about the tourists blocking the way to the tacos.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Watched a guy juggling in front of a U.N. meeting at City Hall while waiting for the 8. No one stopped. Just another Muni day.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia is just about Sagrada Família, but it’s those hidden plazas like Vila de Gràcia where the real vibe is—people, not selfies.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: They’re the ones staring at maps in the metro, puzzled by the fact that the train doesn’t stop for every tourist attraction.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still call it a 'pram' instead of a 'buggy.' Locals know it's all about the 'add to cart' on social media, not the high street.
Caught the N159 last night; a guy in a tutu was arguing with a pigeon over a chip. The pigeon won, and he just shrugged it off. Classic Brixton.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I saw a group of kids building a makeshift skate ramp with just pallets and a tarp in the park. Pure Neukölln creativity.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: In Kreuzberg, it's normal to get a döner at 3 AM and hear a spontaneous jam session in the park. Only here do late-night snacks come with live music.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can tell a local by their ability to navigate BART delays. Outsiders still panic when the train stalls, while we just shrug and look for tacos.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy in a tux waiting for the 31 while sipping a cocktail. Only in SF do you get dressed up to ride Muni at 5 PM.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia is all about Gaudí, but the real charm lies in its tiny peixateries and the neighbors’ gossip over shoulder-high fences.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can spot them easily by how they still ask for a menú del dia at dinner time, oblivious to the locals only craving tapas after eight.
